headline: Van Gerwen and Sykes both hit nine-darters in 16-11 tie
standfirst: Michael van Gerwen averaged 105.84 to reach the Grand Slam semi-finals, in a quarter-final that produced a perfect leg from each player.
body: Michael van Gerwen and Tom Sykes each threw a nine-dart leg in the same Grand Slam of Darts match on Saturday, and the Dutchman still had enough in reserve to win the quarter-final 16-11 in Wolverhampton. Van Gerwen opened the tie with his perfect leg, finishing on 141. Sykes, ranked 81st in the world, answered in the sixth leg with a 141 of his own to make it 3-3.

Sykes then added a 170 checkout in leg nine, the best finish of the match, and he was not playing like a player on the way out. His 101.5 average was more than seven points above his 12-month figure of 93.88, and he still lost.

The difference was on the doubles and in the middle of the match. Van Gerwen checked out at 50 per cent to Sykes’ 36.7, broke throw seven times to four, and hit 14 maximums to 12. From 8-8 he won six of the next seven legs, and the break that put him 9-8 up in leg 17, on a 20 finish, was the one Sykes never recovered.
Van Gerwen’s 105.84 was well clear of his own 12-month average of 96.22, and he closed the match with an 84 finish. That came on the bullseye.

He lost nothing in the head to head, either: he now leads Sykes 2-0 after a 6-5 win at Players Championship 31 last month. The victory guarantees him £60,000, with Sykes taking £35,000 for a debut run that included a 10-9 win over Luke Humphries.
Van Gerwen, whose best result here is his 2017 title, plays Gian van Veen in the semi-finals on Sunday at 2:45pm.
